# University of Jordan
The University of Jordan, established in 1962 by royal decree with King Hussein bin Talal’s support, is the country’s first national university. Its main campus, located in the Jubaiha area north of Amman, spans 1.2 square kilometers and features multiple academic faculties, student facilities, and parking areas. A southern branch campus was opened in Aqaba in 2009 to expand higher education regionally. Early instruction began with the Faculty of Arts, and the university rapidly expanded to include scientific, humanitarian, and medical faculties. It introduced the credit hour system, the first in the Arab world, and offers over 78 undergraduate and more than 140 postgraduate programs organized into scientific, humanitarian, and medical streams. The university maintains academic autonomy and has emphasized research development since the 2000s, registering numerous patents, books, and research papers.
Facilities include the Jordan University Hospital, the country’s first university teaching hospital, accredited for clinical excellence and medical education. The University of Jordan Library is a major resource with over one million items, historical manuscripts, and international documents. It hosts various institutes and centers focusing on archaeology, Islamic studies, photonics, and strategic studies. The university is recognized regionally, holding top national admission scores and ranking within notable international university metrics. It maintains hundreds of international exchange agreements and affiliations with academic organizations across the Arab and global academic community. Notable alumni span politics, science, literature, academia, and international diplomacy, including multiple former prime ministers, cabinet ministers, diplomats, scholars, and professionals distinguished in diverse fields.
